translation_en: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma' al-Duba'i narrated to me: Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Malik, from al-Zuhri, that Malik ibn Aws told him: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab sent for me, and I came to him when the day was well advanced. I found him at home, sitting on a couch close to the sand, leaning on a leather pillow. He said: Malik, some families from your people have arrived, and I have ordered a small gift for them. Take it and divide it among them. I said: If you would appoint someone else to do this, it would be better. He said: Take it, Malik. Then Yarfa' came and asked: Commander of the Faithful, will you receive 'Uthman, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, al-Zubayr, and Sa'd? 'Umar said yes, and admitted them. Then Yarfa' returned and asked whether he would receive al-'Abbas and 'Ali. 'Umar said yes and admitted them. Al-'Abbas said: Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this lying, sinful, treacherous, faithless man. The others said: Yes, Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and relieve them. Malik ibn Aws said: It seemed to me that they had put the two forward for this purpose. 'Umar said: Be patient. I adjure you by Allah, by whose permission the heavens and earth stand: Do you know that the Messenger of Allah said, We are not inherited; what we leave is charity? They said yes. Then he turned to al-'Abbas and 'Ali and adjured them by Allah, by whose permission the heavens and earth stand: Do you know that the Messenger of Allah said, We are not inherited; what we leave is charity? They both said yes. 'Umar said: Allah, Mighty and Exalted, gave His Messenger a special privilege that He gave to no one else. He recited: Whatever Allah granted His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and the Messenger (59:7). I do not know whether he recited the verse before it as well. He said: The Messenger of Allah divided the property of Banu al-Nadir among you. By Allah, he did not keep it for himself instead of you, nor take it to the exclusion of you, until this property remained. The Messenger of Allah used to take from it the maintenance for one year, then make the remainder available as common property. Then he adjured them by Allah, by whose permission the heavens and earth stand: Do you know this? They said yes. Then he adjured al-'Abbas and 'Ali in the same way as he had adjured the others, asking whether they knew this. They said yes. He said: When the Messenger of Allah died, Abu Bakr said: I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah. You two came seeking your inheritance from your nephew, while this man sought his wife's inheritance from her father. Abu Bakr said: The Messenger of Allah said, We are not inherited; what we leave is charity. You considered him a liar, sinful, treacherous, and faithless, while Allah knows that he was truthful, dutiful, rightly guided, and following the truth. Then Abu Bakr died, and I became the guardian of the Messenger of Allah and of Abu Bakr. You considered me a liar, sinful, treacherous, and faithless, while Allah knows that I am truthful, dutiful, rightly guided, and following the truth. I took charge of it. Then you and this man came to me together, united in your affair, and said: Hand it over to us. I said: If you wish, I will hand it over to you on the condition that you make a covenant before Allah to manage it as the Messenger of Allah used to manage it. You both accepted it on those terms. He asked: Is that so? They said yes. He said: Then you came to me asking me to judge between you. By Allah, I will not judge between you on any basis other than that until the Hour is established. If you are unable to manage it, return it to me.
